# Sequence & alignment I/O

Sequences, multiple alignments, FASTQ/BAM/VCF and interval I/O; coordinates/builds

## File-reading paths

Each `Read path` below is relative to the absolute Plugin root given
by the activated entry Skill. Form `file_path` as Plugin root + `/` +
Read path. Use that absolute file path with Read. All Read paths use
this one base, including methods in other groups. The guide is read

## Selection examples

- **Coordinates cross a format or genome-build boundary; BED/VCF/GTF, HGVS, liftover or REF mismatch**: [`genomic-coordinates`](genomic-coordinates/SKILL.md); Read path: `skills/seq-align-io/references/genomic-coordinates/SKILL.md`. Check coordinate convention, assembly and contig names before joining or comparing intervals.
- **Choose SAM/BAM or reference processing methods**: [`bio-alignment-files-sam-bam-basics`](bio-alignment-files-sam-bam-basics/SKILL.md); Read path: `skills/seq-align-io/references/bio-alignment-files-sam-bam-basics/SKILL.md`, [`bio-alignment-files-reference-operations`](bio-alignment-files-reference-operations/SKILL.md); Read path: `skills/seq-align-io/references/bio-alignment-files-reference-operations/SKILL.md`. Choose the relevant SAM/BAM or reference operation; pysam also covers genomic file processing pipelines.
- **Read/write genomic files, extract regions, calculate coverage or run interval operations**: [`pysam`](pysam/SKILL.md); Read path: `skills/seq-align-io/references/pysam/SKILL.md`, [`polars-bio`](polars-bio/SKILL.md); Read path: `skills/seq-align-io/references/polars-bio/SKILL.md`. pysam covers alignment, variant and sequence I/O; polars-bio covers interval operations and genomic file I/O on DataFrames.
- **Read/write/convert multiple sequence alignments (Clustal, PHYLIP, Stockholm, FASTA, Nexus)**: [`bio-alignment-alignment-io`](bio-alignment-alignment-io/SKILL.md); Read path: `skills/seq-align-io/references/bio-alignment-alignment-io/SKILL.md`. Bio.AlignIO handles multiple sequence alignments. SAM/BAM read alignments have separate routes.

## Methods

### bio-alignment-alignment-io

Method: [`bio-alignment-alignment-io`](bio-alignment-alignment-io/SKILL.md); Read path: `skills/seq-align-io/references/bio-alignment-alignment-io/SKILL.md`.
Role: method. Source-declared name: `bio-alignment-io`.

Complete source description: Read, write, and convert multiple sequence alignment files using Biopython Bio.AlignIO. Supports Clustal, PHYLIP, Stockholm, FASTA, Nexus, and other alignment formats for phylogenetics and conservation analysis. Use when reading, writing, or converting alignment file formats.

### bio-sequence-io-paired-end-fastq

Method: [`bio-sequence-io-paired-end-fastq`](bio-sequence-io-paired-end-fastq/SKILL.md); Read path: `skills/seq-align-io/references/bio-sequence-io-paired-end-fastq/SKILL.md`.

### bio-sequence-manipulation-reverse-complement

Method: [`bio-sequence-manipulation-reverse-complement`](bio-sequence-manipulation-reverse-complement/SKILL.md); Read path: `skills/seq-align-io/references/bio-sequence-manipulation-reverse-complement/SKILL.md`.
Role: method. Source-declared name: `bio-reverse-complement`.

Complete source description: Generate reverse complements and complements of DNA/RNA sequences using Biopython, including IUPAC ambiguity codes, gapped alignments, and minus-strand features. ### biopython

Method: [`biopython`](biopython/SKILL.md); Read path: `skills/seq-align-io/references/biopython/SKILL.md`.
Role: toolkit. Source-declared name: `biopython`.

Complete source description: Comprehensive molecular biology toolkit. Use for sequence manipulation, file parsing (FASTA/GenBank/PDB), phylogenetics, and programmatic NCBI/PubMed access (Bio.Entrez). Best for batch processing, custom bioinformatics pipelines, BLAST automation. For quick lookups use gget; for multi-service integration use bioservices.

### genomic-coordinates

Method: [`genomic-coordinates`](genomic-coordinates/SKILL.md); Read path: `skills/seq-align-io/references/genomic-coordinates/SKILL.md`.
Role: method. Source-declared name: `genomic-coordinates`.

Complete source description: Convert genomic intervals between coordinate conventions, normalise and compare variant representations, and detect assembly or contig-naming mismatches before they corrupt an analysis. Use whenever coordinates cross a format, tool, or assembly boundary - converting between BED, GFF/GTF, VCF, SAM/BAM, WIG, PSL, genePred, Picard interval_list, or region strings; reconciling 0-based half-open with 1-based inclusive; left-aligning or trimming indels; checking whether two variant records describe the same change; mapping genomic to transcript, CDS, or protein positions; auditing a BED/GTF/VCF for convention violations; or diagnosing GRCh37 vs hg19 vs GRCh38 vs T2T, chr-prefix, and liftover problems. Triggers include "off by one", "0-based", "1-based", "half-open", "coordinate system", "left-align", "normalize variant", "bcftools norm", "chr prefix", "wrong genome build", "liftover", "REF mismatch", and "HGVS".

Input/context examples (not prerequisites):
- genomic intervals
- variant records

Search terms: off by one, 0-based, 1-based, half-open, left-align, bcftools norm, chr prefix, genome build, liftover, REF mismatch, HGVS.
